tasks.title: rename state cleared on a collective switch and its writes generation-guarded
tasks.redPrompt:
Write the FAILING suite for #297. Contract = `cd ~/workspace-app && gh issue view 297 --comments` — READ ALL COMMENTS. Two amend it: the guard spelling-vs-shape rule, and the two ungated siblings in the same function. Research = `teams/mvox-dev/memory/research/research-297-296.json` (verify.rename). Drift-check every line — this file absorbed #287 (`859f6a4`) and #294 (`c2829ea`).

## The defect, verified at HEAD
All five rename vars are declared ~2655-2665 (`renamingSectionId`, `renameValue`, `renamePending`, `renameError`, `renameStatus`) and **NONE appears anywhere in the route-load `reset` callback** (~155-237). `submitRename` is ~2701-2761. It captures `const g = routeLoad.generation` at ~2725, which is BEFORE its first await (~2731) — a usable capture, NOT the #287 trap. Three ungated writes:
1. `renameStatus = m.roster_section_renamed({ name })` at ~2732 — the success announcement, inside the `try`, no check at all. **This is the primary bug**: a rename confirmed on collective A announces into B's live region.
2. `renameError = { id, name }` at ~2751 — end of the `catch`, unconditional, even though the refetch above it IS guarded with the same `g`.
3. `renamePending = false` at ~2753 — the `finally`, unconditional.

`/roster` is ONE route; a collective switch is a soft nav and the component is never remounted, which is why `$state` survives. Do not write a spec that remounts.

## Pins
1. **NO CROSS-COLLECTIVE ANNOUNCEMENT.** Hold `renameSection`, confirm a rename on A, switch to B, release → the rename status live region is EMPTY. Today it names A's section while B is on screen. Find the region by testid and assert its text content.
2. **NO CROSS-COLLECTIVE ERROR BANNER.** Same but with the write REJECTING → no rename-failure banner against B. `renameError` renders page-level, not row-scoped.
3. **STALE SETTLE DOES NOT CLOBBER A LIVE WRITE.** Start a rename on A, switch to B, start a genuine rename on B, release A's promise → B's controls stay disabled and B's write is not double-fired. This is why guarding the `finally` matters and why clearing on switch alone is insufficient.
4. **CLEARED ON SWITCH.** Whichever of the five are decided to clear (see below) are gone after a switch — assert through rendered state, not the flags (none are exported).
5. **FOCUS STILL LANDS ON A SUPERSEDED SETTLE.** See the constraint below — pin that focus does NOT end up on `<body>` even when the settle is superseded.

## THE CONSTRAINT THAT IS EASIEST TO GET WRONG
`submitRename`'s `finally` does more than clear the flag: it `await tick()` then refocuses the rename trigger (~2757-2759). **That focus work must stay unconditional.** `renamingSectionId` is cleared optimistically at ~2728 so the input unmounts immediately — meaning on ANY settle, superseded or not, focus is already off the input and would fall to `<body>` if the block returned early. So: **gate the flag write, not the block.** An early `return` in this `finally` is a defect, and it also discards a pending return or throw from the `try`. Pin the focus outcome on a superseded settle explicitly — a spec that only checks the flag will pass a fix that drops focus.

## Guard shape and spelling — per the adopted amendment
Shape follows POSITION: early return in `try`/`catch`, conditional write in `finally`. Spelling follows NEIGHBOURS (`routeLoad.isCurrent(g)` and `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` are both live and equivalent — pick what surrounds each site). **Do NOT normalise existing sites** and do not introduce a fourth form.

## Existing specs must stay green
vitest only, no Playwright (`pnpm test`). `src/routes/page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts` (from #287) is the house pattern — read it and reuse its machinery for holding a write and driving a switch. Every existing rename spec asserts current CORRECT single-collective behaviour; if one goes red the fix broke something.

tasks.reviewChecklist:

1. ALL THREE WRITES GUARDED: `renameStatus` success (the primary bug — a rename on A announcing into B), `renameError` catch-write, `renamePending` finally. Fixing only the announcement is a FINDING; fixing only the finally is a FINDING.
2. **THE FOCUS WORK IS STILL UNCONDITIONAL.** Check this specifically — it is the most likely way this ships broken. `submitRename`'s `finally` refocuses the rename trigger after `await tick()`, and `renamingSectionId` is cleared optimistically before the write, so the input is already unmounted on every settle. An early `return` in that `finally` drops focus to `<body>` on a superseded settle AND discards a pending return/throw. Only the flag write may be gated. A guarded-whole-block `finally` is a FINDING even though it looks tidier and will pass a flag-only test.
3. NO SECOND CAPTURE: `g` at ~2725 is usable (before the first await). A newly added entry-level capture alongside it is a FINDING — that was #287's `handleDeactivateConfirm` problem in reverse.
4. SHAPE BY POSITION: early return in `try`/`catch`, conditional write in `finally`. A wrong-shaped guard is a bug, not a style nit.
5. SPELLING BY NEIGHBOURS, and NO NORMALISATION: existing sites unchanged. Cosmetic guard rewrites across the file are a FINDING — they hide the actual fix.
6. PER-VARIABLE RESET REASONING: the five rename vars were decided individually, with reasoning, not cleared reflexively. Silent all-five clearing without stating why is a FINDING; so is ignoring the existing `reset` comment about status vars rather than following or overturning it.
7. SPEC HONESTY: the new specs HOLD THE WRITE and switch mid-write, and assert through rendered state (none of the five is exported). A spec that remounts, or that only holds a reload, cannot fail against the unfixed code — reason about what it would do on `main`.
8. FOCUS PINNED: a spec asserts focus does not land on `<body>` on a superseded settle. Without it, item 2 is unprotected.
9. NO REGRESSION: full suite green, especially #287's `page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts` and #294's join-state specs in the same file.
10. SCOPE: rename state only. `reorderPending`/`reinstatePending`/`deactivateActionError`/`deactivateRefusal` belong to #296 (next task in this run) and the create-path handlers to #299 — touching them here is a FINDING.
tasks.commitBody: Rename state no longer outlives the collective it belongs to. None of the five rename variables were cleared on a collective switch, and three writes in `submitRename` settled without checking the generation the function had already captured: the success announcement, which told a screen-reader user in one collective that a section in another had been renamed; the failure banner, which could appear page-level against a collective the rename never touched; and the in-flight flag, whose unconditional clear could re-enable controls mid-write after a switch. The focus restoration in that same `finally` stays deliberately unguarded — the rename input unmounts optimistically before the write, so every settle, superseded or not, has to put focus back on the trigger rather than leave it on the document body. That is why the flag write is gated and the block is not. Reuses the generation already captured in the function rather than adding a second, and leaves every existing guard site spelled as it was. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills the four stated choices as sentences>.

tasks.redPrompt:
Write the FAILING suite for #296. Contract = `cd ~/workspace-app && gh issue view 296 --comments` — READ ALL COMMENTS. **The scope was AMENDED (issuecomment-5594599579): two ungated siblings folded in.** Research = `teams/mvox-dev/memory/research/research-297-296.json` (verify.reorder, verify.reinstate-error). Drift-check every line — this file absorbed #287, #294, and #297 immediately before this task in the same run.

## Five sites, three functions. They are NOT the same case — treat each on its evidence.

**`reorderPending`** (~2317) — absent from `reset`. Shared by TWO writers, `performReorder` and `performReparent`. Their SUCCESS paths are ALREADY correctly guarded (~2413; ~2543/2548) via captures at ~2396/~2519 that are usable. Only their `finally` blocks (~2432, ~2590) clear unconditionally.

**`reorderError`** (~2326, ADDED BY THE AMENDMENT) — IS cleared in `reset` (~160), but its catch-writes (~2422 in `performReorder`, ~2579 in `performReparent`) are ungated, immediately above refetches that ARE guarded with the same `g`. Renders a PAGE-LEVEL banner, so a stale settle shows a wrong-collective failure banner.

**`reinstatePending`** (~1206) — absent from `reset`, and **`handleReinstate` (~1208-1246) has NO generation capture anywhere.** This is the 'nothing to reuse' case: a new entry-level capture must be added, before the first await. Its `finally` (~1244) and its catch-write (~1242) are both unconditional. Note it is an ID, not a boolean — reason about what that means.

**`deactivateActionError`** (~921) — IS cleared in `reset` (~178). Two writer catches: `handleDeactivateConfirm`'s (~1125), where `gEntry` IS available and usable (captured ~1028, already used correctly by the success path and the `finally` — #287's fix); and `handleReinstate`'s (~1242), where no capture exists at all.

**`deactivateRefusal`** (~910, ADDED BY THE AMENDMENT) — IS cleared in `reset` (~177), but its write in the REFUSAL branch of `handleDeactivateConfirm` (~1064) is ungated. It sits INSIDE the `try`, after two awaits (~1057, ~1058). This is a THIRD ungated write in that function, distinct from the catch the issue originally named.

## Pins
1. **NO CROSS-COLLECTIVE BANNER, per error slot.** For `reorderError`, `deactivateActionError` and `deactivateRefusal`: hold the relevant write, act on A, switch to B, release with a failure/refusal → no banner against B. These are page-level or row-scoped differently — check which, and assert accordingly.
2. **STALE SETTLE DOES NOT CLOBBER A LIVE WRITE**, for `reorderPending` and `reinstatePending`: start on A, switch to B, start a genuine write on B, release A → B's controls stay disabled, B's write not double-fired.
3. **CLEARED ON SWITCH** for the two flags absent from `reset`.
4. **THE REFUSAL BRANCH SPECIFICALLY.** `deactivateRefusal`'s write is reached on the non-error path — a member who cannot be deactivated because they hold a grant. Drive that branch, not just the catch. A spec that only exercises failures misses it entirely.
5. **`handleReinstate` HAS NO GUARD AT ALL** — pin both its settle writes, since neither has any existing protection to lean on.

## Guard shape and spelling
Shape follows POSITION: early return in `try`/`catch`, conditional write in `finally`. **All four amendment sites are in `try`/`catch` bodies, so all four take the early-return shape.** Spelling follows NEIGHBOURS. **No normalisation pass**, no fourth form.

## Existing specs must stay green
vitest only (`pnpm test`). `src/routes/page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts` (#287) is the house pattern for holding a write and switching mid-write. `page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts` and the reorder/arrange suites assert current CORRECT single-collective behaviour — a red one means the fix broke something.

tasks.commitBody: The rest of the roster's in-flight and error state now belongs to the collective it came from. Three functions were involved and they were not the same case. The two reorder writers already guarded their success paths correctly but cleared their flags unconditionally and wrote their failure banner unguarded, one line above a refetch that did check. `handleDeactivateConfirm` had a usable generation and used it for its success path and its settle, yet its refusal branch — the path taken when a member cannot be deactivated because they hold a grant, and so the one an admin is most likely to meet — wrote unguarded after two awaits. `handleReinstate` had no generation captured anywhere, so both of its settle writes needed a new one rather than a reused one. Each `finally` was inspected before being gated rather than guarded wholesale, because the rename fix immediately before this one found a `finally` whose focus restoration had to run on every settle including a superseded one. The two create-path handlers, which have no guard machinery at all and can insert a section into a collective it does not belong to, are deliberately left to #299.
